attributes.body_ja:
「ばかりだ」は、「だけ」という意味（いみ）を持（も）つ副助詞（ふくじょし）の「ばかり」と助動詞（じょどうし）の「だ」（または「です」）からできています。これを、動詞（どうし）の連体形（れんたいけい）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）うと、「(A) だけが起（お）きている」ことを表（あらわ）します。また、この表現（ひょうげん）には、「(A) だけがどんどん進（すす）んでいる」や「(A) だけがずっと続（つづ）いている」というようなニュアンスもあります。

ほとんどの場合（ばあい）、「ばかり」は変化（へんか）を表（あらわ）す動詞（どうし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。例（たと）えば、「高（たか）くなる」や「低（ひく）くなる」、「強（つよ）くなる」や「弱（よわ）くなる」、「良（よ）くなる」や「悪（わる）くなる」、「早（はや）くなる」や「遅（おそ）くなる」などです。

「ばかり」のあとに文（ぶん）が続（つづ）くとき、「だ」は連用形（れんようけい）の「で」に変（か）わります。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

この「ばかり」は、物事（ものごと）が悪（わる）い方向（ほうこう）に進（すす）んでいるときに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。ただし、これは文法（ぶんぽう）のルールではないので、良（よ）い変化（へんか）に使（つか）う場合（ばあい）もあります。
attributes.body:
Occasionally, the adverbial particle ばかり is combined with verbs in their attributive form, to show that (A) is the only thing that is occuring. It may also imply that (A) is happening 'more and more', or that 'it keeps on (A)'. This phrase utilizes ばかり's standard meaning of 'only', and combines it with the auxiliary verb だ (or です).

As can be seen with these sentences, this use of ばかり is paired almost exclusively with verbs that describe some form of change (higher/lower, stronger/weaker, better/worse, faster/slower, etc).

If the speaker would like to express further information in a (B) part of the sentence, だ will simply get changed to its conjunctive form で, before continuing.

Caution

This use of ばかり is primarily seen with negative trends. However, this is not a grammatical rule, and positive trends may also sometimes appear with ばかりだ.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Expressing the opposite of 「だけ」 with 「ばかり」

attributes.body: ばかりだ attaches to the dictionary (non-past) form of a verb and is used to show that an action, often a negative one, keeps happening or is the only thing happening. In contrast, てくる combines the て-form of a verb with くる to describe an action that began in the past and has continued to the present. Unlike ばかりだ, てくる can be used for both positive and negative situations.

attributes.body: つづける and ばかりだ both show continuation, but with different nuances. つづける attaches to verb stems and shows simple ongoing action, e.g. 減り続けている 'is continuing to decrease'. ばかりだ adds the sense of 'more and more,' often negatively, e.g. 減るばかりだ 'keeps on decreasing'.

second_relatable.title: ばかりだ
second_relatable.meaning: (Only) continue to, Keep on -ing, More and more

attributes.body: ばかり means 'only' or 'just', often suggesting repetition or excess, e.g. 文句ばかり言っている ('He does nothing but complain.'). ばかりだ builds on that to express that a situation continues to worsen or progress in one direction, e.g. 状況は悪くなるばかりだ ('The situation keeps getting worse.').

second_relatable.title: ばかりだ
second_relatable.meaning: (Only) continue to, Keep on -ing, More and more

attributes.body: ばかりだ and 一方だ are similar in that both express continuous or progressive change. However, ばかりだ is typically used with negative developments and often carries a more subjective tone, e.g. 状況は悪くなるばかりだ ('The situation keeps getting worse'). 一方だ, on the other hand, sounds more neutral or objective, and doesn't necessarily imply a negative trend, e.g. 人口は増える一方だ ('The population keeps increasing').
